summary:
[  edit  ]
The Touch In  CHOP  can be used to create a high speed connection between two TouchDesigner processes via CHOPs.
Data is sent over TCP/IP. The Touch In  CHOP  (client) receives its data from a  Touch Out CHOP  (server). The Touch In  CHOP  is similar to a  Pipe In CHOP  but highly optimized for TouchDesigner-to-TouchDesigner communication. For interfacing with other software or devices, see the  Pipe In CHOP  or the  TCP/IP DAT .
To receive network data from another "server" computer (e.g. from a Touch Out  CHOP  running remotely), a connection must be established between the server and the Touch In  CHOP  before data is sent.
The data is received as time slices, and can be used to eliminate frame dropping if the sender or receiver is not running at its target frame rate. See  Time Slicing  and the  Time Slice CHOP . Can also be run non-time sliced to receive full channel data.
To analyze the timing of the messages coming in, attach an  Info CHOP  to the Touch In  CHOP . It will show the internal queue size and whether it is dropping or missing data ( queue_advanced_total  and  queue_retarded_total  should not be increasing, and  queue_length  should not be zero).
NOTE for Windows OS - If experiencing connection issues, confirm Windows Firewall is disabled for TouchDesigner.
See also:  OSC In CHOP

parameters.label: Protocol
parameters.name: protocol
parameters.description: ⊞  - Selects which network protocol to use to transfer data. Different protocol's have methods of connecting and using the address parameter. For more information refer to the  Network Protocols  article.

parameters.label: Multi
parameters.description: Cast Messaging (UDP)   multicastmsging  -

parameters.label: Address
parameters.name: address
parameters.description: The computer name or IP address of the server computer. You can use an IP address (e.g.  100.123.45.78 ) or the computer's network name can be used directly. If you put " localhost ", it means the other end of the pipe is on the same computer.

parameters.label: Network Port
parameters.name: port
parameters.description: The network port of the server.

parameters.label: Active
parameters.name: active
parameters.description: While on, the  CHOP  receives information from the pipe or server. While off, no updating occurs. Data sent by a server is lost, but a pipe will store the data until  Active  is turned on again. If in Network mode, turning this parameter on initiates a connection, and turning it off breaks the connection.

parameters.label: Queue Target
parameters.name: queuetarget
parameters.description: The target queue length the  CHOP  will attempt to maintain.

parameters.label: Queue Target Unit
parameters.name: queuetargetunit
parameters.description: Choose between using Samples, Frames, or Seconds as the units for this parameter.

parameters.label: Queue Variance
parameters.name: queuevariance
parameters.description: The range around the Queue Target that's acceptable. If the queue's length is within the target and variance range, the  CHOP  will not bother to adjust the queue length.

parameters.label: Queue Variance Unit
parameters.name: queuevarianceunit
parameters.description: Choose between using Samples, Frames, or Seconds as the units for this parameter.

parameters.label: Maximum Queue
parameters.name: maxqueue
parameters.description: The maximum size of the queue when full. Incoming samples will be dropped if the maximum queue is reached.

parameters.label: Max Queue Unit
parameters.name: maxqueueunit
parameters.description: Choose between using Samples, Frames, or Seconds as the units for this parameter.

parameters.label: Queue Adjust Time
parameters.name: adjusttime
parameters.description: Specifies how often to repeat/drop a samples in order to get closer to the queue target range. If the value = 1 and the units = seconds, then it will try to repeat/drop a sample once per second to maintain the queue target set in the  Minimum Target  and  Maximum Target  parameters above.

parameters.label: Adjust Unit
parameters.name: adjusttimeunit
parameters.description: Choose between using Samples, Frames, or Seconds as the units for this parameter.

parameters.label: Recover Outside Range
parameters.name: recover
parameters.description: If the queue size goes outside of the target size range for more than the 'adjust time', then if this option is on it will stop delivering new data or throw away a lot of data, until queue size is back in the middle of the min/max target. If this option is of the queue size will be slowly inched towards the target size instead (by dropping or repeating single frames every once in a while).

parameters.label: Use Synced Ports
parameters.name: syncports
parameters.description: ⊞  - This parameter lets you send the the data in a single global pipe if required. This can be important if various data streams must be sent in frame sync. For more information, refer to  Touch In/Out Synced Ports .

parameters.label: Off
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: Uses separate ports for each port number assigned.

parameters.label: On
parameters.name: on
parameters.description: Uses a single global pipe for all Touch Out CHOPs using this Transfer Port Type. The global pipe uses port 10500 internally to send all the global port type data together at once. The Network Port parameter is still used to determine which Touch In  CHOP  gets the data on the receiving side.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page.

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Index
parameters.name: datindex
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the index of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
parameters.name: datname
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the name of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Channel Name is  Path : Parameter
parameters.name: autoname
parameters.description: The channel is the full destination of where to export to, such has  geo1/transform1:tx .

parameters.label: Export   Root
parameters.name: autoexportroot
parameters.description: This path points to the root node where all of the paths that exporting by  Channel Name is  Path : Parameter   are relative to.

parameters.label: Export  Table
parameters.name: exporttable
parameters.description: The  DAT  used to hold the export information when using the  DAT  Table  Export  Methods (See above).

parameters.label: start
parameters.description: Start of the  CHOP  interval in samples.

parameters.label: length
parameters.description: Number of samples in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: sample_rate
parameters.description: The samplerate of the channels in frames per second.

parameters.label: num_channels
parameters.description: Number of channels in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: time_slice
parameters.description: 1 if  CHOP  is  Time Slice  enabled, 0 otherwise.

parameters.label: export_sernum
parameters.description: A count of how often the export connections have been updated.

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

parameters.label: samples
parameters.description: per-second of a  CHOP . Each CHOP in your network has a sample rate. In contrast, the overall timeline has a  Frame Rate , which is the number of frames to  cook  and display per second, generally your monitor display frequency, default 60.

parameters.label: An  Operator Family  that manipulates text strings: multi
parameters.description: line text or tables. Multi-line text is often a python  Script  or  GLSL  Shader, but can be any multi-line text.  Tables  are rows and columns of cells, each containing a text string.

parameters.label: TouchDesigner is a hierarchy of components. "root" is the top
parameters.description: most network in the hierarchy. The  Network Path  or Path for root is simply  / . A typical path is  /project1/moviein1 .
